scope: All Commonwealth terrestrial travel paths, across seven Atlas physical zones; not a blanket prohibition on existing bridges, docks, quays, buildings or private interior/yard finishes.
rule: Unpaved, location-specific terrain paths; no asphalt/concrete paved carriageways, painted traffic lanes or modern highway guardrails as generic road dressing. Natural exposed bedrock is not paving. Engineered crossings and other existing structures retain their established identities.

regional_wayfinding_and_edge_protection.authority: Direct Founder continuation: no paved roads, all terrained paths based on location wthin atlas; get creative with markings and modern guardrails within world guidelines.
regional_wayfinding_and_edge_protection.interpretation: Preserve navigation and edge-protection functions using locally grounded visual analogues. Proposed fixtures are not exact route placements, engineering designs, or new permanent canon.
design_rules: No painted traffic lanes, asphalt, concrete carriageway or generic galvanized W-beam highway guardrail.
Use regional materials, age, maintenance and terrain-specific hazard context; not every path has markers or protective rails.
Markings are freestanding or carved features, not painted pavement. Existing approved structures remain distinct.
Vehicles remain permitted within scoped approval, but road suitability and exact vehicle reference still require review.

regional_designs.surface: Exposed bedrock, loose scree, worn high-pass track
regional_designs.markings: Stacked stone cairns and tall notched stakes visible above seasonal snow
regional_designs.protective_edges: Rough stone parapets at established exposed crossings; timber posts and iron chain where appropriate

regional_designs.surface: Compacted loam, gravel, forest litter and pasture track
regional_designs.markings: Carved wooden direction posts and fieldstone edge markers
regional_designs.protective_edges: Split-rail timber fencing and low dry-stone walls only where terrain or land use warrants

regional_designs.surface: Alluvial earth, clay, loose gravel and seasonal wheel ruts
regional_designs.markings: Worn stone waymarkers with simple carved direction glyphs; taller posts near flood-prone approaches
regional_designs.protective_edges: Low fieldstone edges or stout timber railings near established river crossings

regional_designs.surface: Dusty earth, broken rock and flattened grassland tracks
regional_designs.markings: Weathered upright stone markers and widely spaced timber stakes
regional_designs.protective_edges: Low stacked stone boundaries or ranch-style timber rails near actual hazards; open stretches remain unfenced

regional_designs.surface: Rain-dark earth, exposed roots, loose gravel and bedrock
regional_designs.markings: Pale stone waymarkers and weathered timber posts with restrained iron fittings; no painted road lines
regional_designs.protective_edges: Short rugged timber-and-forged-iron edge rails or low stone walls at real drops; no generic continuous steel highway rail

regional_designs.surface: Raised earthen causeways, wet mud and established timber crossings
regional_designs.markings: Tall flood-height posts with carved bands and pole markers visible above water
regional_designs.protective_edges: Weathered timber railings and stout posts at established raised crossings; keep waterways and drainage open

regional_designs.surface: Compacted coastal earth, loose gravel, sand and exposed rock
regional_designs.markings: Carved stone direction markers and maritime-style timber posts near existing port approaches
regional_designs.protective_edges: Stone parapets or timber-and-rope boundaries at established quay or exposed edge; no implication of a new coastal route

regional_wayfinding_and_edge_protection.g06: Unplaced visual study: rain-dark natural track, worn stone marker, short weathered timber/iron protective edge only if a real drop is visible. No route name, island horizon, paved surface, or truck identity claim.
